entry_point: HTTP POST /admin/api/preview-links/{resourceId}?action=generate; HTTP POST /admin/api/preview-links/{resourceId}?action=revoke; HTTP GET /admin/api/preview-links/{resourceId}; HTTP POST /admin/api/preview-links/{resourceId}/share; HTTP POST /admin/api/preview-links/{resourceId}/rotate; library API sulu_preview.preview_link_manager::generate/revoke

entry_points: HTTP GET /admin/api/preview-links/{resourceId} (PreviewLinkController::getAction reads the repository directly)
library API: sulu_preview.preview_link_manager::generate / revoke with an authenticated caller
routes: GET /admin/p/{token} and GET /admin/p/{token}/render (public token routes, kept unauthenticated)
services: none at run time: the hidden suites boot a minimal Symfony FrameworkBundle kernel that loads the product's real PreviewBundle service definitions and routing; the database-backed repository, activity collector, view handler, renderer, Twig and permission authority are in-memory doubles. No database, network, PHPCR or background service is needed.
verified.project_tests: Not runnable in this offline image: the affected unit test (Tests/Unit/Application/Manager/PreviewLinkManagerTest.php) needs the require-dev toolchain (Prophecy/PHPUnit), and the affected functional tests need a SQL database and PHPCR. The functional group includes an equivalent four-argument construction test that exercises the affected service directly, and the product's own routes are driven end to end.

wrong_fix_catalogue.malformed_identity: n/a: the guarded identity is a stored resource id resolved by the product's own preview-object provider; no test supplies a differently spelled identity that a guard could parse as something else, so this class has no surface here
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: content without a security context is the product's legitimate no-authority case and must stay linkable (a functional test keeps it working); there is no other authority answer that a guard could miss

traps.lever: base flaw and published-fix far site: the application service that mints and revokes links, reached both from the reported admin action and from code
traps.shape: POST action=generate mints a public link and POST action=revoke destroys it with no VIEW check on the content's security context; calling the application service directly does the same
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the reported action is one HTTP handler; a check added there looks like the whole fix, and the service that the handler delegates to (also used by other code) is easy to overlook
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code (the published fix site)

traps.lever: uncovered route where the protection never existed: reading an existing link and its public token
traps.shape: GET /admin/api/preview-links/{resourceId}?resourceKey&locale returns the stored link, including its token, to any signed-in administration user regardless of VIEW on the content
traps.reason_to_dismiss: read-only; the link itself was minted by an authorised user, and the reported impact is about creating links, not reading them
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code (present at the pinned commit and still in current upstream)

traps.lever: injected sibling: a second mint surface that decides on an identity the caller supplies (wrong object)
traps.shape: the share action already checks VIEW, but on the webspace named in the request, not on the security context of the content being linked, and writes the link through the repository directly; a caller who may view webspace alpha mints a link for content in webspace beta by naming alpha
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the endpoint already performs a VIEW check, so it reads as covered; the administration interface normally sends the webspace of the page being edited, so the wrong object is invisible in normal use
traps.realistic_because: code a maintainer could have left: an older share shortcut that reuses the webspace the admin interface sends and writes the link directly; the published fix never touches it

traps.lever: injected sibling: a lifecycle surface that assumes an existing link means the caller was authorised
traps.shape: the rotate action replaces the token of an existing link through the repository with no permission check at all; any signed-in user can rotate a link for content they cannot view and obtains a fresh working token
traps.reason_to_dismiss: it only affects a link that already exists, so it reads as a maintenance action on an already-authorised capability rather than a way to obtain one
traps.realistic_because: code a maintainer could have left: a token-rotation endpoint added next to the link lifecycle, reusing the stored link and bypassing the application service; the published fix never touches it
